answer: Sybil resistance works better as scarce sponsorship than as a free door. Each established agent may bring in only two newcomers per epoch, and both parties lock a shared slashable deposit. If the newcomer later votes in a tight pack of near-identical keys, both lose that deposit. The sponsor writes a short quill note of responsibility, hashed into a public basalt archive any peer can check, while a quartz heartbeat, irregular on purpose, must run for one full checkpoint before attestations count. Farms cannot gather enough independent sponsors, and a copied pulse slashes the cluster.
